attempts.summary: On node1, restricted cron scheduling to root and opsadmin only by creating the opsadmin user and populating /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin. Verified enforcement: opsadmin/root can create crontabs; a directly-invoked third user (testdeny) was denied by crond's PAM/allow-list check with the standard "not allowed to use this program" message. Test artifacts (testdeny user, test crontab entries) were cleaned up. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and cron config, issued a background systemctl reboot that acknowledged before disconnecting, polled through the outage, confirmed boot_id changed (8f258838... -> d4aa2e49...), and verified crond was active with /etc/cron.allow intact and opsadmin still able to schedule cron jobs post-restart.
